blocks.text: Bubblegum Coquette is a variation of Coquette that incorporates elements of the Bimbocore and Babygirl aesthetics. It is a coquette substyle that is more suggestive than most, while still focusing on youth, girly 2000s nostalgia, toy and candy motifs, and bright pink.

The Bubblegum Coquette aesthetic juxtaposes cute, childish innocence with the burgeoning libido of young adulthood. This is portrayed visually through the pairing of cute, youthful imagery (candy, toys, sparkles, braces) with more explicit imagery (lingerie, adult content stars, high heels, etc).

The Bubblegum Coquette style dates back to the mid 2010s on Tumblr, where it rose alongside the Nymphet aesthetic. As young women began to adopt the Nymphet trope, some found that they connected less with the tragic elements of that aesthetic, and more so with the overt sexuality. Though the visuals weren't always sexual in nature, more often than not, blogs focused on Bubblegum Coquette were also heavily associated with fetishlife. These Tumblr accounts posted Nymphet-adjacent visuals and kink-related visuals together, focusing on bright colors and youthful motifs. At this time, there was no agreed-upon name for the aesthetic.

The style was retroactively named “Bubblegum Nymphet” by YouTuber Nymphet Fashion in a 2018 video, which she described as an attempt to "desexualize the word "nymphet" and show the fashion is separate from any kink." In this video, Nymphet Fashion dressed in the typical Bubblegum Coquette style, with a pink miniskirt, a white 'Lolita' tank top and pigtails, while also speaking about the separation between sex and style, and how Nymphet styles do not need to be inherently sexual. The name was adopted by the community used throughout the late 2010s. As the community dropped the word "nymphet" in favor of "coquette" due to ongoing censorship issues with Tumblr and Pinterest, the switch from Bubblegum Nymphet to Bubblegum Coquette came naturally.

The visuals of Bubblegum Coquette collocate childlike imagery with eroticized images. The color palette is hyper-feminine, consisting of shades of pink and purple, white, pastels, and light blues. Common motifs are sweets (particularly lollipops, ice cream, bubblegum and cotton candy), childhood cartoons such as My Little Pony, Hello Kitty, and Disney Princesses, sparkles/glitter, braces and pigtails. Other common visuals are typical childhood interests, like rollerskates, jump rope, hopscotch, playgrounds and stuffed animals. These things are sometimes paired with suggestive imagery, like a focus on lips/tongues, women in clothing that is too small/revealing, and sometimes even censored stills from adult films or censored photos of adult content creators.

The look can be described as a mixture between typical Coquette, Babygirl, and Bimbocore. The fashion adheres pretty strictly to the visuals and color palette. Alongside the candy motifs, you will also see stripes, plaid, polka dots, and fruit patterns -- typically strawberries or cherries. It is common to also see cartoons/mascots represented on the clothing, frills, lace and bows, and butterflies and unicorns. Skirts are worn both high- and low-waisted, but jeans are typically low-waisted.
V-necks and other low cut tops
Hair in pigtails, ponytails, loose curls and braids
Sugary sweet/gourmand and fruity-floral scents, like Prada Candy, Ariana Grande Sweet Like Candy, Britney Spears Fantasy, Juicy Couture 2006, and Victoria's Secret Love Spell
Hair bows, hair clips, barrettes and ballies
Candy in general, particularly pinwheel/swirly lollipops

Like Coquette and Nymphet proper, Bubblegum Coquette faces criticism for sexualizing youth and youthful imagery. Popular Bubblegum Coquette figures like Belle Delphine have been accused of "pedo baiting" due to the combination of provocative and childlike imagery and the usage of DDLG in explicit content. This community also overlaps with pro-ana/thinspo circles, as do all coquette aesthetics, and face criticism for the lack of body diversity and promotion of thinness/smallness in both imagery and community.
As the themes and visuals of this aesthetic can be upsetting, viewer discretion is strongly advised.
